classification.classification_note: Stage 01 reproduced an ASan heap-buffer-overflow read in `_zend_is_inconsistent` / `zend_hash_find`. The source-level bug is compile-time attribute validation passing a non-NULL class scope into constant evaluation; for the witness `parent::\xff` attribute argument this permits `zend_get_constant_ex()` to take the `parent` branch and query `scope->parent`'s constant table during compilation.

bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in Zend hash lookup: zend_hash_find_bucket (Zend/zend_hash.c) performs an out-of-bounds read when resolving attribute/constant values during attribute validation (zend_get_attribute_value / validate_attribute in Zend/zend_attributes.c). This out-of-bounds access can corrupt memory or crash the process and may be exploitable.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / staged patch diff
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness is the exact 44-byte PHP source `<?#[Attribute(parent::\xff)]class \xff extends \xff{}`. During class compilation, `zend_compile_class_decl()` records the new class in `CG(active_class_entry)` and then calls `zend_compile_attributes()` for the class attribute list. `zend_compile_attributes()` stores the attacker-controlled attribute argument `parent::\xff` as a constant AST in `attr->args[0].value`. Vulnerable `validate_attribute()` then calls `zend_get_attribute_value(&flags, attr, 0, scope)` with a non-NULL `scope = CG(active_class_entry)`, so `zval_update_constant_ex()` resolves that stored constant AST under class scope during compilation. `zend_ast_get_constant_name(ast)` produces the full constant name string `parent::\xff`, and inside `zend_get_constant_ex()` that name is split into `class_name = "parent"` and `constant_name = "\xff"`. Because `class_name` is `parent` and `scope` is non-NULL, the resolver takes the `parent` branch, sets `ce = scope->parent`, and performs `zend_hash_find_ptr(&ce->constants_table, constant_name)`. The saved ASan report shows the resulting out-of-bounds read in `_zend_is_inconsistent` / `zend_hash_find` when that hash table is checked. The patch fixes this by changing `validate_attribute()` to call `zend_get_attribute_value(&flags, attr, 0, NULL)`, which prevents scoped `parent::...` resolution during this compile-time validation pass.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. Attribute validation resolves the first argument using the current class scope instead of `NULL`, so a `parent::...` constant AST is resolved through `zend_get_constant_ex()` under class scope during compilation.
root_cause.note: Commit `f06afc434aec631f18f8da8ffca9a6f0559e1acf` changes this call to `zend_get_attribute_value(&flags, attr, 0, NULL)`, with an inline comment that the class is not fully linked yet and may be in an inconsistent state.

sink.description: Unsafe read site on the reproduced path. After `zend_get_constant_ex()` takes the `parent` branch and looks up `constant_name` in `scope->parent`'s constant table, `zend_hash_find()` checks that selected hash table with `IS_CONSISTENT(ht)`, and the saved ASan report places the out-of-bounds read in `_zend_is_inconsistent` from this macro expansion.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant value is the stored constant AST built from the witness attribute argument. Validation copies that AST out of `attr->args[0].value` immediately before attempting constant resolution.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admitted continuation after the parser has accepted a class declaration with a class attribute. Reaching this call means the witness was parsed as a class declaration carrying `decl->child[3]` attributes and compilation advanced into class-attribute validation.

fine_trace.note: Source. While compiling the class attribute list, the attacker-controlled argument AST `parent::\xff` is converted into a stored constant AST in `attr->args[0].value` for later validation.
Before attribute validation runs, class compilation records the new class entry as the active scope. The later validator receives this non-NULL `scope`.
The accepted class declaration carries a class attribute, so class compilation enters the attribute-validation pass while `CG(active_class_entry)` is still the current class scope.
Root cause. The validator forces the first attribute argument to a value using non-NULL `scope` instead of `NULL`. The patch changes this call to pass `NULL`.
Validation copies the stored constant AST for the first attribute argument out of `attr->args[0].value` into `ret`, preserving the attacker-chosen constant expression for resolution.
Because the copied attribute value is still a constant AST, constant updating extracts the full constant name string `parent::\xff` from that AST.

Constant updating calls `zend_get_constant_ex()` with the full constant name string and the same non-NULL class scope from step 4, making compile-time attribute validation perform scoped constant resolution.

Inside constant resolution, the full name is split at `::` into `class_name = "parent"` and `constant_name = "\xff"`. This is the missing source-level transition from the AST name string to the later lookup key.
Because `class_name` is `parent` and `scope` is non-NULL, the resolver takes the `parent` branch and selects `scope->parent` as the class entry whose constants table will be queried.
The resolver performs class-constant lookup in the selected parent class entry using the split `constant_name` key. The saved crash stack proves this lookup path reached `zend_hash_find_ptr()`.

Sink. `zend_hash_find()` checks the selected constant-table hash object, and the saved sanitizer trace reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read in `_zend_is_inconsistent` from this consistency test.

poc.trigger: The saved witness is the exact 44-byte PHP source `<?#[Attribute(parent::\xff)]class \xff extends \xff{}`. Compiling that file reaches class-attribute validation, passes a non-NULL `scope` into `zend_get_attribute_value()`, resolves the stored `parent::\xff` constant AST under class scope, takes the `parent` branch in `zend_get_constant_ex()`, and then reaches the crashing `zend_hash_find_ptr(&ce->constants_table, constant_name)` path.
